message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), water freezes at roughly **–20 °C**.  

This is derived from the water phase diagram: as pressure drops below atmospheric, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the melting/freezing temperature decreases. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –20 °C (the exact value depends slightly on the purity of the water, but –20 °C is a good approximation).
